title: Pilot scope: load profile synthesis, QPS sampling & success metrics - Foxbridge Labs

Foxbridge to provide 2 weeks of anonymized request logs and average token length breakdown by 2025-11-04
Schedule on-prem networking checklist call (SE + Foxbridge infra) for 2025-11-10
Follow-up meeting to review benchmark results and finalize pilot SLA on 2025-11-13

summary: Discovery and POC scoping focused on workload characterization: target QPS/concurrency, token-length distribution, tail latency SLOs, and a 4-week pilot with three benchmark phases. Key risks: bursty episodic traffic, VPC networking constraints, and security review timeline.
topics: Workload sampling and synthetic traffic generation
Success criteria & KPIs (p95/p99 latency, error rate, cost per 1k tokens)
Networking and security constraints for Private deployment
questions: What are the realistic QPS peaks vs sustained?
How many concurrent sessions hold KV cache state?
What's acceptable p95 and p99 latency for user-facing flows?
Can Foxbridge provide representative request logs?
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-30 15:00 PT | Duration: 62m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Koh (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Foxbridge Head of ML), Daniel Wu (Platform), Priya Nair (SRE), Owen Harris (PM)

Summary auto-note (auto): high-level scope for workload profiling and pilot KPIs.

00:00 - Maya: hey everyone thanks for carving out the time. quick intro from our side — im maya, i run enterprise at redwood inference. today we want to lock down traffic shape, success criteria, and a realistic pilot timeline.
00:18 - Lena: hi — lena here. we have a couple of production endpoints used by our customer support assistant and an internal insights tool. both shapes are different so we wanted to do a combined pilot.
00:30 - Ethan: placeholder, i'll lead the bench plan — my goal is to get an apples-to-apples throughput & tail-latency comparison across hosted vs private.
00:42 - Owen: timeline constraint: we want a pilot completed before holiday freeze, ideally results by mid-nov so product can sign off.
00:50 - Daniel: quick stack overview — we currently call an internal GPT-style model behind an api gateway. avg sustained qps is around 8 during business hours, spikes to ~120 for promotional blasts, and we see concurrency up to 60 for some agents workflows. token lengths vary a lot.
01:12 - Priya: and we have strict egress rules; private deployment needs peering and a managed k?m key. also SOC2 documentation is required for procurment.
01:30 - Maya: ok that helps. can you share a histogram of input and output tokens? even rough percentiles will be enough for synthetic generation.
01:40 - Lena: yes, we can share a redacted histogram. expect med input ~ 45 tokens, outputs avg 180 but with a heavy tail, we have episodes that produce 800+ tokens.
01:58 - Ethan: that tail is important — it drives KV cache pressure and increases latency. for benchmarking we usually model three mixes: short (<64 in/out), medium (64-256), and long (256+ with episodic bursts).
02:18 - Owen: what about success metrics — we care most about p95 latency for user-facing suggestions (should be under 300ms) and p99 under 1s for noncritical jobs.
02:30 - Maya: noted. from redwood's product playbook we typically scope pilot SLOs as: p95 < 250ms for small prompts at 50 QPS sustained, p95 < 400ms for mixed prompts at 20 QPS sustained, and p99 < 1.2s across the board. but that's flexible.
02:50 - Daniel: can you map that to cost? our CFO wants cost per 1k tokens as a gating metric.
03:00 - Ethan: we'll produce cost-estimates from the benchmark traces — we measure GPU utilization, tokens/sec, and amortized cost. we'll give a delta between hosted and private infra.
03:12 - Lena: one wrinkle: we have conversational sessions that maintain KV cache per session, roughly 30% of requests hit the cache state. how do you simulate that?
03:24 - Ethan: we have a workload harness that simulates session affinity and KV warm/cold ratios. we'll drive synthetic QPS with a configurable cache-hit distribution. we should match your observed 30% warmed state.
03:40 - Priya: network latency matters — our agents are in eu-west-1 and we have cross-region hops. can redwood simulate WAN latency in the bench?
03:50 - Ethan: yes, we can add an artificial network delay model. for private/pvpc tests we'll want to run a baseline inside your network to measure e2e.
04:02 - Owen: ok let's break down the benchmark phases.
04:08 - Ethan: phase 0: ingest and synthesis — Foxbridge supplies 14 days of anonymized logs and token histograms; Redwood ingests and generates synthetic workload definitions. phase 1: microbenchmarks — single-client latency & throughput for the three prompt mixes. phase 2: scaled QPS runs — ramp to target sustained QPS and run burst windows to validate tail. phase 3: production replay and verification — run a 24h replay if possible.
04:36 - Maya: realistic durations?
04:40 - Ethan: plan: data handoff (1 week), microbench (3 days), scaled runs (1 week), replay & verification (up to 1 week). entire pilot 3–4 weeks.
05:00 - Lena: that fits our internal timeline. key success criteria: p95 kept under agreed thresholds during sustained windows, no >0.5% error rate, and verified failover to a smaller quantized model with <2x latency increase.
05:20 - Daniel: we also want a heatmap of concurrency vs token-length to help size caches and batch windows.
05:28 - Ethan: we'll produce QPS-concurrency contour plots and token-length heatmaps; those inform batch size and kernel selection for the runtime.
05:40 - Priya: on security: we need KMS integration (customer-managed), audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and SSO. how long does that usually take?
05:50 - Maya: for Private deployments KMS + SSO onboarding usually takes 2–3 weeks once we have contact from your sec team. audit log forwarding can be enabled earlier for a subset of events.
06:04 - Owen: competitors question — we evaluated Anthropic and saw better out-of-the-box latency but higher cost. we're curious how Redwood's batching & caching compare.
06:15 - Ethan: our continuous batching and prefix/KV caching typically provides 20–40% cost reduction for conversational workloads compared to naive endpoints, but depends heavily on session locality and token mix. we'll validate with your logs.
06:34 - Lena: what about cold-start tail latency on long sequences?
06:40 - Ethan: long sequences increase memory pressure; we measure stepwise: cold KV cache vs warm, and long-token sessions often require different kernel paths. for benchmarks we'll isolate those and run long-token-only bursts.
06:56 - Maya: let's capture concrete acceptance criteria so procurement can sign off.
07:04 - Owen: acceptance items: 1) sustained 20QPS mixed prompts p95 < 350ms, 2) ability to handle 200QPS spikes with degraded but acceptable p95 < 900ms, 3) error rate <0.5% over pilot, 4) documented cost per 1k tokens for expected workload, 5) private deployment passes basic security checklist (KMS, SSO, audit logs).
07:32 - Daniel: that's reasonable. what's the test harness topology for private? do you need inbound ports opened?
07:40 - Ethan: we prefer outbound-only, with VPC peering and an egress rule to Redwood's ingestion endpoints. for on-prem we can also run a local agent that pulls model shards — we'll capture both options.
07:58 - Priya: any nonfunctional constraints? we need to keep PII strictly out of benchmark payloads.
08:04 - Maya: absolutely. transmission will be anonymized. we'll also sign an addendum if needed.
08:14 - Lena: about the synthetic generator — can we bias for episodic bursts like weekly reports that create long outputs?
08:23 - Ethan: yes, we'll parameterize episodic frequency and burst magnitude; we'll run scenarios with 1% of requests being long-episode 600-1000 tokens to match what you described.
08:38 - Owen: cost modelling -- can we get a baseline cost delta for hosted vs reserved capacity?
08:45 - Maya: yes, Redwood will provide model-level cost curves; we'll show per-1k-token estimates for the three mixes and an estimate for reserved GPU amortization.
08:58 - Daniel: how do you measure tokenization differences? our tokenizer is slightly different from open-source defaults.
09:05 - Ethan: we can ingest your tokenizer map or sample outputs and compute tokenization ratios. that's part of data handoff.
09:18 - Maya: ok next, communications plan and deliverables. after your log handoff, we'll ingest and return a workload spec and a draft benchmark plan. then we'll run the microbench and share a results deck.
09:32 - Priya: timeline for security review again? two weeks after we hand over contact details?
09:36 - Maya: yes roughly 10–15 business days for the standard SOC2/KMS onboarding for private; some items like audit-log forwarding are faster.
09:46 - Lena: are there any known failure modes we should be aware of during replay?
09:50 - Ethan: replay can expose stateful behavior — session affinity mismatches will show up as cache-miss spikes; network jitter can amplify tail latency. we'll flag those in the report and recommend mitigations (sticky sessions, backpressure windows).
10:12 - Owen: let's document the specific metrics we'll collect: p50/p95/p99 latencies, errors per minute, tokens/sec, tokens/request distribution, GPU utilization, batch sizes, KV hit ratio, and network e2e latency.
10:30 - Maya: agreed. we'll also provide a lightweight cost model spreadsheet that maps tokens/sec to cost per hour under different reserved capacity scenarios.
10:40 - Daniel: one more question on rollout: if the pilot passes, how long to stage to prod?
10:45 - Maya: typical cadence — pilot results + tuning (2 weeks), small canary (1 week), wide rollout (dependent on app but usually 2–4 weeks). so 5–7 weeks after pilot signoff.
10:58 - Lena: procurement note — we need pricing sheet and security docs attached to the follow-up email so our vendor team can pre-clear.
11:06 - Maya: will attach.
11:10 - Ethan: technical note — for the scaled runs we'll test both mixed-model routing and a fallback small-quantized variant to validate graceful degradation. we'll capture latency multipliers for fallback.
11:26 - Priya: can you show sample graphs you plan to deliver?
11:30 - Ethan: yes sample: qps vs p95 contour, token-length CDF, concurrency heatmap, KV hit-over-time, and cost per 1k tokens table.
11:42 - Owen: ok this is good. final ask from our side: include a clear go/no-go checklist after the replay so we can quickly decide.
11:50 - Maya: we'll include a go/no-go template and recommended gating thresholds.
11:58 - Lena: thanks, team. 
12:02 - Maya: next steps recap: we'll send benchmark harness and runbook (Maya), ethan will produce synthetic generator config and run initial microbench, foxbridge to hand off logs and tokenizer sample by 11/04. follow-up results review 11/13.
12:20 - Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: some speaker attribution may be approximated, timestamps are approximate. there are occasional filler words and overlaps in natural conversation.
